claims: On Election Night 1860, Lincoln was nominated as the Republican candidate for President.
Lincoln received 231-1/2 votes on the third ballot of the Republican convention, which was not announced.
An Ohio delegate announced a change of four Ohio votes from Chase to Lincoln, leading to a surge of support for Lincoln.
The crowd at the convention erupted in joy upon the announcement of Lincoln's nomination.
Lincoln was in Springfield during the convention and received the news of his nomination via telegram.
The news of Lincoln's nomination spread quickly, leading to celebrations in Chicago and beyond.
Lincoln was officially elected President of the United States on February 13, 1861, after receiving a majority of the electoral votes.

claims: South Carolina was the first state to secede.
Fort Sumter commanded Charleston Harbor and became the focus of national interest.
Major Anderson decided to abandon Fort Moultrie and defend Fort Sumter.
Lincoln found the government in a chaotic condition upon taking office.
Lincoln's purpose was to hold the remaining slave states in the Union.
Lincoln promised to hold the United States forts and not to be the aggressor.
Major Anderson was beleaguered in Fort Sumter with 76 combatants and 128 total men.
Lincoln decided to send provisions to Fort Sumter.
General Beauregard commanded the military forces and sent a summons to Major Anderson to surrender.
On April 12, 1861, General Beauregard opened fire on Fort Sumter, marking the beginning of the war.
The garrison of Fort Sumter surrendered on April 14, 1861.
The fall of Fort Sumter was hailed with delight in the South and caused a storm of indignation in the North.
Lincoln had been in office less than six weeks at the time of the fall of Fort Sumter.

claims: The Gettysburg Address was delivered by Abraham Lincoln at the dedication of the Gettysburg cemetery on November 19, 1863.
Lincoln's part in the event was to pronounce the formal words of dedication, while Edward Everett was the main orator.
Lincoln wrote the Gettysburg Address on a sheet of foolscap paper during busy moments leading up to the event.
The address is described as prose in form but poetic in effect, with many rhythmical sentences.
The audience was impressed by Lincoln's gravity and solemnity during the address, with many moved to tears.
The Gettysburg Address begins with the phrase 'Fourscore and seven years ago' and emphasizes the founding principles of the nation.
Lincoln's speech reflects on the sacrifices made by soldiers and calls for dedication to the unfinished work of the nation.
The speech concludes with a vision of a government 'of the people, by the people, for the people' that shall not perish from the earth.
The immediate effect of the Gettysburg Address was not significant.

Lincoln composed the Gettysburg Address while traveling from the White House to the battlefield.
The Gettysburg Address emphasizes the principles of liberty and equality, stating that the nation was conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal.
Lincoln stated that the living should be dedicated to the unfinished work of those who fought at Gettysburg.
The address concludes with a call for a new birth of freedom and a government of the people, by the people, for the people.

Lincoln stated that there was less occasion for an extended address than there was at his first inauguration.
Lincoln expressed that the progress of the war was well known and hoped for a satisfactory future.
He reflected on the anxiety surrounding the impending civil war at his first inauguration and the current state of the nation.
Lincoln noted that one eighth of the population were colored slaves localized in the southern part of the Union.
He acknowledged that the issue of slavery was somehow the cause of the war.
Lincoln believed that neither party anticipated the magnitude or duration of the war.
He suggested that the cause of the conflict might cease with or even before the conflict itself should cease.

claims: The assassination of President Lincoln occurred at Ford's Theatre.
Lincoln was shot at the back of the head on the left side.
The bullet passed through Lincoln's brain and stopped just short of his left eye.
Lincoln was carried to a room in a house opposite the theatre after being shot.
Lincoln died at twenty-two minutes after seven o'clock in the morning following the assassination.
John Wilkes Booth was the assassin who shot Lincoln.
Booth shouted 'Sic semper tyrannis!' after jumping onto the stage.
Booth was recognized as an actor of melodramatic characters.
Booth was aided in his escape by Edward Spangler, an employee at the theatre.
Booth's leg was broken when he fell onto the stage after the assassination.
At the same time as Lincoln's assassination, an assault was made on Secretary Seward.
The conspiracy to assassinate Lincoln involved multiple active members and had been planned for months.
Seven men and one woman were charged with being involved in the conspiracy after the assassination.
The military commission found the accused guilty of conspiracy related to Lincoln's assassination.

Lincoln received a substantial majority of the electoral vote, totaling 180 to 123.
Lincoln's popular vote was approximately 930,170 against him, indicating nearly a million votes more against him than for him.
Fifteen states did not give Lincoln any electoral votes, and in nine states, he received no popular votes.
The election was determined largely on sectional lines, with slavery as the primary issue.
Lincoln's election was aided by an unexpected division in the Democratic party.

The address emphasized the principles of liberty and equality, stating that the nation was conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal.
Lincoln stated that the living should be dedicated to the unfinished work of those who fought at Gettysburg.
The address concluded with a call for a new birth of freedom and a government of the people, by the people, for the people.
The audience was deeply moved by Lincoln's words, with many in tears during his delivery.

claims: Abraham Lincoln and Mrs. Lincoln attended Ford's Theatre on the evening of April 14, 1865, to watch the play 'The American Cousin.'
General Grant declined Lincoln's invitation to accompany him to the theatre.
Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre at approximately half-past ten o'clock.
John Wilkes Booth, the assassin, shouted 'Sic semper tyrannis!' after shooting Lincoln.
Booth escaped from the theatre after the assassination.
Major Rathbone was present in the President's box during the assassination and attempted to apprehend Booth.
Lincoln was carried across the street to a house after being shot, where he was attended by surgeons and friends.
Lincoln died at approximately seven o'clock in the morning on April 15, 1865.
Secretary Seward and his son were also attacked on the same night as Lincoln's assassination.
The news of Lincoln's assassination caused widespread grief and mourning across the country.

claims: The Presidential election took place on November 6, 1860.
On Election Night, November 6, Lincoln sat alone with the operator in the telegraph box at Springfield, receiving the results of the elections of Presidential electors in various States.
Lincoln was sure of his return before the election returns were complete.
Lincoln solved the first problem of his Presidency, the choice of a Cabinet, before leaving the telegraph box.
Lincoln was elected by a minority of the American people, having a large majority over Douglas but potentially losing to Douglas if Breckinridge's votes were considered.
Lincoln's votes were drawn only from the Northern States, carrying almost all the free States and no others.
The election of Lincoln was greeted throughout the South with a howl of derision.

claims: Lincoln was confronted with the decision regarding Fort Sumter shortly after his inauguration.
Major Anderson at Fort Sumter reported to Lincoln that he could only hold out a few weeks longer unless reinforced.
General Scott advised Lincoln that relieving Fort Sumter would require a force of 20,000 men, which was not available.
Lincoln's Cabinet was divided on whether to provision Fort Sumter, with some members supporting it and others opposing it.
Lincoln reserved his decision on whether to evacuate Fort Sumter despite the Cabinet's recommendations.
The Confederacy claimed Fort Sumter as part of their sovereign rights.
Lincoln's eventual decision was to send provisions to Fort Sumter but not troops.
The Confederate batteries opened fire on Fort Sumter on April 12, 1861.
Anderson capitulated on April 14, 1861, after the fort became untenable.

claims: The Gettysburg Address was delivered by Abraham Lincoln on November 19, 1863.
The occasion was the dedication of a National Cemetery on the field of Gettysburg.
Edward Everett delivered a two-hour oration at the dedication ceremony.
Lincoln was invited to say a few words at the close of the ceremony.
Lincoln's speech is described as having the potential to endure with the English language.

Lincoln's address included the phrase 'Four score and seven years ago our fathers brought forth on this continent a new nation, conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal.'
Lincoln's speech emphasized the importance of dedicating the ground to the soldiers who died in the Civil War.

claims: Abraham Lincoln delivered his Second Inaugural Address on March 4, 1865.
The Second Inaugural Address is noted for its use of intense religious language.
Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address reflects his desire for mercy and reconciliation.
The Second Inaugural Address emphasizes the need to bind up the nation's wounds and achieve lasting peace.
Lincoln expressed in the Second Inaugural Address that the war was a divine punishment for the offense of slavery.
The Second Inaugural Address includes the famous line, 'With malice toward none; with charity for all.'
Lincoln believed that the judgments of the Lord regarding the war were true and righteous.

claims: Abraham Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre on the night of April 14, 1865.
Lincoln fell forward upon the front of the box unconscious and dying after being shot.
John Wilkes Booth entered Lincoln's box unobserved and shot him.
Booth attempted to stab Major Rathbone, who tried to seize him.
Booth jumped from the box to the stage, fell, and broke the small bone of his leg.
Booth shouted 'Sic semper tyrannis' after jumping to the stage.
Booth escaped on a horse that was waiting at the stage door.
Booth was the leader of a conspiracy that aimed to kill not only Lincoln but also Andrew Johnson and William H. Seward.
One of the conspirators attacked Seward at his home, wounding him and others.
Booth was later shot in a barn by soldiers pursuing him.

claims: Robert S. Chew left Washington at 6 P.M. on April 6, 1861, and arrived at Charleston, S.C. on April 8, 1861.
Fort Sumter had neither been surrendered, evacuated, nor attacked at the time of Chew's arrival.
Chew requested an interview with Governor Pickens upon his arrival in Charleston.
Governor Pickens received a copy of the orders from Chew and stated he would submit it to General Beauregard.
General Beauregard was in charge of military operations in the vicinity of Fort Sumter.
Chew was not authorized to receive any communication in reply from Governor Pickens.

extractions.author: Abraham Lincoln
claims: The Gettysburg Address was delivered during the American Civil War.
The address references the founding of a new nation conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal.
Lincoln states that the nation is engaged in a great civil war testing its endurance.
The address was delivered at a battlefield where soldiers died for the nation.
Lincoln emphasizes that the ground cannot be consecrated by words, as the brave men who fought there have already hallowed it.
Lincoln expresses that the living should dedicate themselves to the cause for which the fallen soldiers gave their lives.
He resolves that the dead shall not have died in vain and that the nation shall have a new birth of freedom.
Lincoln concludes that government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth.

extractions.author: Abraham Lincoln
claims: Abraham Lincoln delivered his Second Inaugural Address on March 4, 1865.
The only known manuscript of Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address is a fair copy rather than a composition draft.
Lincoln revised the ending of the address by pasting a slip of paper over the last two lines and writing the revised version on it.
Printed copies of the address were made available to the press.
The manuscript was presented by Lincoln to John Hay and later to the Library of Congress in 1916.
Lincoln's address acknowledged that there was less occasion for an extended address than at his first inauguration.
Lincoln noted that during his first inauguration, there was an impending civil war that all sought to avert.
Lincoln stated that one eighth of the whole population were colored slaves localized in the Southern part of the Union.
Lincoln claimed that the cause of the war was related to the interest in slavery.
Lincoln expressed hope for a lasting peace among all nations.
